speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and fungal esophagitis places him at high risk for opportunistic ocular infections. Given your specific symptoms of floaters and black spots without pain, have you noticed any color desaturation or a "smoke screen" effect in your vision? REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopy_Right_Eye.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. The combination of severe immunosuppression (AIDS), risk factors for opportunistic infections (fungal esophagitis, Kaposi's sarcoma), unilateral decreased vision, and painless black spots/floaters is classic for this diagnosis.
